# Docky 1.0.6
- Clipboard history now automatically captures supported clipboard changes while Docky is running; no Save clipboard button is needed. Automatic capture is on by default and can be paused in Clipboard settings. - A strict maximum of 15 unique entries is applied to new captures and restored history. The oldest item is removed when full; the existing 30 MB total size limit also applies. - Click an item to copy it back to the clipboard and move it to the top. Copying the same content from another app also promotes the existing entry without creating a duplicate. - Finder file and folder copies retain native file references so they can be copied back into other apps. Original files remain in place. - Docky ignores its own clipboard writes and skips clipboard content marked concealed, transient, or automatically generated. Automatic capture pauses while locked or macOS Secure Input is active. - Clipboard Quick Action now opens history. The shelf shows its item count out of 15; individual removal, clear-all, and expiry controls remain available.
## Validation
Debug and universal Release builds; isolated native pasteboard checks for text/file round-trips, concealed-content exclusion, own-write tracking, duplicate promotion, restored-history deduplication, expiry, and 15-item eviction; existing shelf, display, and collapse checks. Tests do not inspect the user's general clipboard. Developer ID signing, notarization, and hosted installer byte verification run through publish.sh. Cross-app clipboard monitoring and row clicking still need interactive validation on target Macs.
